program.help:
Remove waveforms with hardware-dropout channels from spike data.
Examines every spikeDetection group and removes any spike waveform where one or more channels are entirely flat — either all-zero (ADC cutout / hardware disconnection) or stuck at a constant non-zero value (railed amplifier / DAC fault).
Must run AFTER ndm_extractspikes or ndm_extractspikes_sdiff and BEFORE ndm_pca / ndm_klustakwik.
Original .res, .spk, .fet, and .clu files are backed up to <session>_spikecleaner_backup/ before modification.
DETECTION CONDITIONS
CUTOUT — every sample on a channel is exactly zero. This is the unambiguous signature of an ADC dropout or a broken wire clamped to the rail by the amplifier.
FLAT — every sample on a channel has the same value (variance == 0 after DC removal). Catches amplifiers stuck at a non-zero constant. Controlled by removeFlatChannels (default: on).
PARAMETERS
# removeFlatChannels
Set to 1 to remove waveforms where any channel has zero variance (constant value, possibly non-zero). Set to 0 to detect only all-zero channels (default 1 — recommended).
# dryRun
Set to 1 to report how many spikes would be removed per group without modifying any files. Useful for assessing data quality before committing (default 0).
